... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then that was an entertaining first innings but that is just the half. The other half will begin when the hosts try to chase down the target while the visitors give it their all to defend it. Do you think West Indies will be able to chase down 326 on the board? We will find out soon.

Harry Brook is in for a chat. He says that he had to give himself time out there. Shares that the surface is a little bit tough and slow at times. Mentions that the batting was tough in the middle phase. States that they have been practicing the sweep shot over the last couple of days during their practice session. Further adds that they did not quite know what the surface was going to be like. Feels that it is nice to be here after a poor World Cup. Reckons that 325 is a good total and they should be good if they change it up with the ball.

The West Indies bowlers will be happy about their comeback after the first 10 overs. Gudakesh Motie and Alzarri Joseph managed to stop the destructive opening pair and after that, the other bowlers showcased their skills and took some timely wickets. Romario Shepherd struck at a very crucial time right when Harry Brook had decided to be aggressive along with Liam Livingstone. Shepherd dismissed both of them putting his team back in the game. They will need to work on their death bowling but the way their bowlers worked as a unit in the middle phase was commendable. They ended up bowling out the Englishmen. Gudakesh Motie was the pick of the bowlers as he bowled economically and took a couple of wickets as well.

England had a great start thanks to the explosive batting by Phil Salt and Will Jacks. However, after their dismissal, Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett could not build a good partnership. Harry played a heroic and sensible innings to bring his team back into the game. Jos Buttler struggled a lot out in the middle and he will look to regain his form as soon as possible. However, Brook’s cautious batting kept the scoreboard running and along with the help of Liam Livingstone, Sam Curran, and Brydon Carse they managed to cross over the 300-run mark. At the end of the innings and after losing all their wickets, England en up with 325 runs in the bag.

What an eventful first innings it was. Maybe that was the trailer of the action we will get to see going further in this match and the series. England had a strong start but the middle phase of the innings was dominated by the hosts. A few timely wickets put them back in the game. However, the Englishmen have managed to power themselves to 325.

We are moments away from the start of the first ODI, but before that, the two teams and match officials will line up for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Antigua and Barbuda first followed by the national anthem of England and then the West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is pitchside. He says that the dimensions are pretty equal on all sides and that the average first innings score is around 240. It is a new pitch and it will be a little uncertain in nature. Samuel Badree joins him and says that there are patches of bounce in critical areas. He mentions that it is a hard surface and as the ball gets older the viewers will get to see some runs.

West Indies skipper, Shai Hope says that they were looking to bowl first. Mentions that it is a decent and fresh wicket. Further adds that there will be some early moisture which should help them. Feels that it is important to take every game and series as they came. Shares that every game has points to play for. Informs that they are going with two spinners and Sherfane Rutherford will be making his ODI debut.

The captain of England, Jos Buttler says that they will bat first and he mentions that it is a pretty good wicket to make full use of their batting strength. He adds that he has a lot of talent in the group and this series will give exposure to the young guys and they should have fun. Informs that Ollie Pope, John Turner, Matthew Potts and Tom Hartley are the ones missing out in this game.

Despite recent setbacks, the England and Wales Cricket Board places its trust in Jos Buttler's leadership, designating him to lead a squad notably lacking key players like Joe Root, Dawid Malan, Jonny Bairstow, Mark Wood, and Ben Stokes. This creates an opportunity for a young and untested ensemble to step up and showcase their potential on the international stage. The batting lineup features the reliable Test opening partnership of Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett, with the responsibility to provide strong starts. The middle order, comprising Harry Brook, Phil Salt, and skipper Jos Buttler, forms a formidable core. Supporting them are emerging talents like Gus Atkinson and Brydon Carse, complemented by the experience of Sam Curran. Rehan Ahmed takes on the crucial role of the leading spinner, adding balance to the squad. West Indies, on the other hand, grapples with the disappointment of not qualifying for the recent World Cup. Shai Hope assumes leadership responsibilities, leading a squad that includes uncapped players Sherfane Rutherford and Matthew Forde. The return of opener Kjorn Ottley marks a notable inclusion, but the absence of Shane Dowrich, who announced his immediate retirement, is a significant development. The batting order heavily relies on the trio of Brandon King, Alick Athanaze, and Shimron Hetmyer to shoulder the run-scoring responsibilities. The pace attack will be led by Alzarri Joseph, a potent force in home conditions, with support from Oshane Thomas and Romario Shepherd. In the spin department, Yannic Cariah is expected to play a key role. As these cricketing powerhouses prepare to lock horns, historical head-to-head records favour England, but the absence of key players introduces an element of unpredictability. Weather forecasts hint at the possibility of rain and overcast conditions, adding further intrigue to the series. The anticipation is palpable as fans await the outcome of this closely watched contest. The question that resonates is who will seize an early lead in this highly anticipated ODI series between England and West Indies? The answer unfolds soon on the Caribbean cricketing stage, promising an enthralling battle between bat and ball.
